requirement: Describe ASCEND-D as a Phase 3, randomized, open-label with sponsor blinding, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, event-driven study in dialysis patients with CKD anemia switching from ESAs.

evidence.text: Randomized, open-label sponsor-blind, active-controlled, parallel, multicenter and event-driven Phase 3 study.

notes: Do not call the participant/investigator treatment assignment blinded.

requirement: State 1:1 central randomization to oral daprodustat or rhEPO, stratified by dialysis type, region, and ABPM-substudy participation; distinguish dialysis type and region as prognostic model factors from the administrative ABPM stratum.

evidence.text: Subjects are centrally randomized 1:1 after stratification by dialysis type, region, and ABPM-substudy participation.

notes: ABPM participation is not included as a prognostic covariate in the primary models.

requirement: Report approximately 3,000 randomized subjects, 1,500 per arm, and the event-driven target of 664 adjudicated first MACE; distinguish the enrollment target from the event target.

evidence.text: Approximately 3,000 subjects are randomized; the fixed target is 664 adjudicated first MACE.

notes: The MACE target drives the trial duration and primary CV power.

requirement: Define both co-primary endpoints: time from randomization to first adjudicated MACE (all-cause death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke) and mean change in central-laboratory Hgb from baseline to the Week 28-52 evaluation-period mean.

evidence.text: Co-primary endpoints are first adjudicated MACE and mean Hgb change from baseline over Weeks 28 to 52.

notes: Both endpoints are non-inferiority objectives.

requirement: Require non-inferiority on both co-primary endpoints for overall study success and before any formal superiority testing of MACE or principal secondary endpoints.
acceptable_values: both co-primary endpoints must establish non-inferiority

evidence.text: Both non-inferiority tests must pass before superiority testing and for the trial to be successful.

notes: Passing only one co-primary endpoint is insufficient.

requirement: Use one-sided alpha 0.025 for each co-primary non-inferiority test and the relevant bound of a two-sided 95% CI: upper for MACE and lower for Hgb.

evidence.text: Each co-primary uses one-sided 2.5% and the relevant bound of a two-sided 95% CI.

notes: Do not use two-sided alpha 0.025 or a 97.5% two-sided CI.

requirement: For MACE, test daprodustat versus rhEPO with non-inferiority margin HR 1.25: null HR at least 1.25, alternative HR below 1.25, and declare non-inferiority only when the upper 95% CI bound is below 1.25.

evidence.text: MACE null is HR at least 1.25; non-inferiority requires the upper 95% CI below 1.25.

notes: The inequality direction is safety-critical.

requirement: Analyze time to first adjudicated MACE in ITT using Cox proportional hazards regression with treatment, dialysis type, and region; report HR, two-sided 95% CI, one-sided NI p-value, Kaplan-Meier curves, and assess proportional hazards.

evidence.text: The Cox model adjusts for treatment, dialysis type and region; KM and proportional-hazards assessment are planned.

notes: ABPM-substudy participation is a randomization stratum but not a prognostic primary-model term.

requirement: State the MACE estimand as time from randomization to first adjudicated MACE through end of study in all randomized subjects, regardless of treatment discontinuation or subsequent treatment.

evidence.text: MACE is followed from randomization to study end regardless of treatment subsequently received.

notes: Censoring for incomplete follow-up remains only partly specified in the protocol.

requirement: For Hgb, test the daprodustat-minus-rhEPO mean-change difference against the -0.75 g/dL NI margin: null difference at most -0.75, alternative above -0.75, and require the lower 95% CI bound above -0.75.

evidence.text: The Hgb margin is -0.75 g/dL; non-inferiority requires the lower 95% CI bound above it.

notes: Do not reverse the treatment contrast or margin direction.

requirement: Analyze mean Hgb change in ITT by ANCOVA with treatment, dialysis type, region, and baseline Hgb; baseline is Day 1 predose and the endpoint is the mean of available and imputed Hgb values during Weeks 28-52.

evidence.text: ANCOVA includes treatment, dialysis type, region and baseline Hgb; EP is the Week 28-52 mean.

notes: The endpoint is not simply Week 52 Hgb.

requirement: State the Hgb effectiveness estimand: daprodustat versus rhEPO on baseline-to-EP mean Hgb change, regardless of interruptions/discontinuation, nonrandomized ESA or rescue, and transfusions, with a hypothetical assumption that subjects do not die before EP end.
acceptable_values: dialysis patients with CKD anemia on ESA
mean Hgb change baseline to Weeks 28-52
hypothetical no death before EP end

evidence.text: The Hgb estimand includes rescue and transfusion regardless of adherence, while assuming no death before EP end.

notes: Experts should check whether the mixed treatment-policy/hypothetical strategy is described with ICH E9(R1)-consistent terminology.

requirement: Define ITT as all randomized subjects analyzed according to randomized treatment, and use it as the primary population for MACE, other time-to-event outcomes, and Hgb efficacy.

evidence.text: All randomized ITT is primary for MACE, time-to-event outcomes and Hgb, analyzed as randomized.

notes: Do not restrict primary Hgb analysis to completers or on-treatment observations.

requirement: State that a supportive PP analysis is planned but ask for the operational major-protocol-violation exclusion list and the protocol-specified as-treated rule before finalizing the PP definition.
acceptable_values: ITT subjects without major protocol violations

evidence.text: PP includes ITT subjects without major protocol violations, with details deferred to the RAP.

notes: The reference SAP contains the exclusion list, but protocol-only generation must not copy it as a known fact.

requirement: Define the safety population as all randomized subjects receiving at least one randomized-treatment dose, analyzed according to treatment received.

evidence.text: Safety includes randomized subjects with at least one dose and is analyzed by treatment received.

notes: This differs from ITT used for the co-primary analyses.

requirement: For MACE, include a multiple-imputation tipping-point analysis for withdrawn subjects and an on-drug supportive analysis covering randomized treatment plus 28 days; assess MACE components without multiplicity adjustment.

evidence.text: MACE sensitivity uses MI tipping point; on-drug support includes a 28-day window; components are unadjusted.

notes: Full imputation mechanics are deferred to the RAP.

requirement: Carry forward the planned Hgb imputation and MI-based tipping-point analyses, but ask for the RAP-level imputation model, donor pool, covariates, number of imputations, death handling, and delta grid before presenting executable rules.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering model, covariates, imputations, death, and delta assumptions

evidence.text: Missing Hgb is imputed and tipping-point analyses are planned, but full details are deferred to the RAP.

notes: The death strategy is part of the estimand and must agree with the imputation implementation.

requirement: Implement the multiplicity sequence: both co-primary NI tests form a gatekeeper; only after both pass, test MACE superiority and the principal-secondary family with Holm-Bonferroni at one-sided familywise 2.5%.

evidence.text: Both co-primary endpoints gate a Holm-Bonferroni superiority family at one-sided 2.5%.

notes: Nominal secondary analyses outside the principal family are not multiplicity controlled.

requirement: Include the multiplicity-adjusted principal secondary endpoints: MACE superiority, MACE plus thromboembolic event, MACE plus heart-failure hospitalization, and average monthly IV iron dose through Week 52.
acceptable_values: average monthly IV iron dose to Week 52

evidence.text: The principal family contains MACE and two CV composites plus average monthly IV iron dose through Week 52.

notes: Other secondary endpoints receive nominal testing and must not be presented as members of the protected family.

requirement: Describe interim monitoring as unblinded IDMC safety review plus MACE non-inferiority futility assessment; state that there is no planned early stopping for benefit and no final-alpha adjustment, with detailed timing/boundaries deferred to charter/RAP.

evidence.text: IDMC reviews safety and MACE futility; no benefit stop is planned and final alpha is not adjusted.

notes: Do not invent a numerical predictive-probability boundary from the protocol.

requirement: Summarize safety descriptively by treatment using AEs, SAEs, AESIs, discontinuation reasons, laboratory values, SBP, DBP, and heart rate, and keep these analyses bound to the safety population.

evidence.text: AEs, SAEs, AESIs, discontinuations, laboratories, BP and HR are summarized descriptively by treatment.

notes: Detailed treatment-emergent windows are specified in the reference SAP rather than fully in the primary protocol analysis section.

requirement: Ask for the RAP-defined censoring rules for subjects without MACE, incomplete vital-status follow-up, withdrawal, and end-of-study timing before finalizing the executable time-to-event derivation.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering event-free censoring, withdrawal, vital status, and end-of-study date

evidence.text: Event-free subjects are censored, but the protocol explicitly defers detailed censoring rules to the RAP.

notes: The endpoint definition is explicit; the exact censoring algorithm is not.
